answer: Each agent deposits a unique onyx‑signed token that is minted only after it proves continuous contribution to the network’s river of tasks, verified by a rotating inlet of auditors. The protocol applies quadratic weighting: the influence of an identity grows with the square of its token stake, so thousands of cheap sybils add only marginal weight while a single well‑staked node commands full power. An attacker must acquire enough genuine tokens to outweigh the quadratic penalty, costing resources comparable to the value of the protected services.
